title: A constant sheaf across a dense normal open
statement:
Let $Y$ be a Noetherian
normal integral
scheme, let $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ be a nonempty
open immersion,
and let $M$ be a finite module. The canonical map
$\underline M_Y\to v_*\underline M_V$, with
direct image on the
etale sites, is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $\Lambda$ for the commutative coefficient ring of $M$ and put $F=\underline M_Y$ in the category of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$, as in [def-constructible-constant]. By [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], normality of $Y$ says that each local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. Thus $Y$ is integral with integrally closed local rings, and $v$ is a nonempty open immersion, exactly as required for the normal-open unit theorem. No additional hypothesis on $M$ or $v$ is introduced.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-constant-generic-open-unit] with $j=v$ and the given $\Lambda$-module $M$. It gives an isomorphism $\eta_v(F):F\xrightarrow{\sim}v_*v^{-1}F$, where $\eta_v$ is the adjunction unit of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. The cited theorem is for arbitrary modules and does not require Noetherianity, so in particular applies to the finite module and Noetherian scheme in this item.

proof.text: Use the pullback-of-constants isomorphism of [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] in module coefficients. To specify its canonical comparison $\gamma_v:v^{-1}F\to\underline M_V$, the adjunctions in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and [def-constructible-constant], and the section formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], give, naturally in any module sheaf $G$ on $V$, $\operatorname{Hom}(v^{-1}F,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,v_*G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda}(M,\Gamma(Y,v_*G))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda}(M,\Gamma(V,G))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\underline M_V,G)$. Define $\gamma_v$ by the element corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{\underline M_V}$. The reverse bijections define its inverse: naturality shows that each composite corresponds to the identity of its source. In particular, the adjoint of $\gamma_v$ is $c=v_*(\gamma_v)\circ\eta_v(F)$, and the constant-sheaf adjunction sends $c$ to $M\to\Gamma(V,\underline M_V)$, $m\mapsto$ the constant section with value $m$. By the same adjunction this characterizes the canonical map of the statement. Direct image is a functor by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], so $v_*(\gamma_v^{-1})$ is inverse to $v_*(\gamma_v)$: their composites are the images of the corresponding identity maps. The inverse of $c$ is therefore $\eta_v(F)^{-1}\circ v_*(\gamma_v^{-1})$, proving the required isomorphism of module sheaves on the small etale site.
